Subject: Eunoia discovery — evaluation artifacts, model recommendations & quant tradeoffs

Hi Sophia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our side.

Call summary (30 min):
- Goal: evaluate candidate open models for question-answering (customer support domain) at 99th percentile throughput ~50 req/s, median latency target for first-token < 120ms, typical responses ~400–600 tokens.
- Constraints: PII redaction pipeline, on-prem pilot preferred (VPC later), procurement window H1.

Recommended immediate deliverables (we can provide these this week):
1) Lightweight prompt set & ref responses (attached: eunoia_prompt_set_v1.json) — covers FAQ, follow-up clarification, and long-context extraction.
2) Micro-benchmark instructions (attached: microbench_instructions.md) — how to run the 10-minute local test we recommend.
3) Quantization trade study (attached preview: awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoffs.xlsx) — concise summary and per-model expected quality delta vs throughput gains.

Initial model recommendations for your QA/POC:
- Baseline (quality-first): redwood-rlhf-13B (FP16) — highest fidelity, baseline latency/cost for your prompts.
- Performance candidate (cost/throughput): redwood-13B-awq (AWQ-4bit, per our tests gives ~2.5–3x throughput vs FP16 at ~1–3% average EM/Exact-match drop depending on prompt).
- Hybrid option: open-30B-gptq (GPTQ-4bit) — often matches AWQ for throughput, slightly better on long-context coherent answers but shows more variance on rare factuals.

Key quality questions we flagged for today:
- What is the minimum acceptable drop in task-specific accuracy (EM / F1) relative to your current API?
- Are there classes of queries where hallucination tolerance is higher (e.g., internal docs) vs customer-facing answers?

Suggested next steps:
- We’ll drop the prompt set, instructions, and trade spreadsheet into the Drive link in this thread.
- If you’re good, propose a 2-week POC where we run the microbench on your sample data, then a canary rollout to a dedicated pool.
- Technical deep-dive with our inference engineer (Marissa) to align on KV cache, batching tolerances, and any payload encryption needs — 45 minutes.

Proposed times for the deep-dive (PST): Monday 1/11 10:00–10:45, Monday 1/11 15:00–15:45, Tuesday 1/12 09:00–09:45. Let me know what works and I’ll send the invite.

Attachments: eunoia_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt/label pairs), awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoffs.xlsx (summary + per-model charts), microbench_instructions.md

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

For the POC we can start with a smaller synthetic load, but please confirm what "~2.5–3x throughput" vs FP16 maps to in absolute latency for our typical responses (400–600 tokens).

2) Quality tolerance: for customer-facing answers we need <2% decrease in EM/F1 vs our current vendor on the FAQ set; internal answers can tolerate up to 5% drop. We’ll provide a labeled subset to check this.

3) Data handling: we need confirmation that KV cache and logging can be disabled or routed to our VPC — any PII will be scrubbed pre-flight. Also provide a short list of SOC2 artifacts you can share for procurement.

4) Question on AWQ vs GPTQ: does AWQ produce deterministic outputs for the same seed/prompt? We observed variance in some compressed runs with other vendors.

We’re generally aligned on the 2-week POC. If you can send the microbench instructions and the trade spreadsheet, we’ll review and come back with a labeled FAQ subset by COB Monday.

Thanks — Sophia

Hi Sophia — thanks for the quick note and the quality guardrails. Short answers inline and next steps below.

1) Absolute latency: from our AWQ lab runs using the microbench (A100-80GB, batch=16, token stream):
- redwood-rlhf-13B (FP16): ~3.2 ms/token (baseline)
- redwood-13B-awq (AWQ-4bit): ~1.1 ms/token (~2.9x throughput improvement)
- open-30B-gptq (GPTQ-4bit): ~1.3 ms/token
For a 500-token response that maps roughly to 550–600 ms end-to-end on AWQ in the baseline network conditions; your observed network variance will add to this. We’ll include these cells in the benchmark report link.

2) Quality tolerance: AWQ in our internal evals tends to show a small, concentrated degradation on adversarial or very long-chain reasoning prompts (1–3% EM/F1 on those slices). For FAQ-style Q&A we often see <1% delta. GPTQ can sometimes reduce the sharpness of rare factual recall but shows better behavior on extended generation. FP8 (experimental) can deliver FP16 parity on many metrics but requires tuned kernels and is currently limited to specific deployment configs.

3) Determinism: AWQ and GPTQ determinism depends on kernel scheduling and RNG seeding. With deterministic serving configuration (fixed seeds, disabled dropout) outputs are reproducible for the same prompt and cache state. We’ll provide a small deterministic-run checklist in the microbench instructions.

4) SOC2 / evidence: we can share SOC2 type II summary, encryption-in-transit docs, and an audit log sample. Procurement pack arriving with the POC docs.

Deep-dive: let’s lock Mon 1/11 15:00–15:45 PST — that works for Marissa, Aditya and me. I’ll send the calendar invite and include a short agenda: 1) microbench walkthrough (10m), 2) trade spreadsheet highlights (15m), 3) integration/POC plan & success criteria (15m), 4) Q&A (5m).

Attached: awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoffs.xlsx (full sheet), microbench_instructions.md, eunoia_prompt_set_v1.json

—Laura
